item.description:
### Network
- A new **Network** section answers "is it my Wi-Fi, my internet, or the service?" It draws your connection from this Mac to your router, your provider and the internet, each with its latency, so a slow hop stands out, and leads with a plain verdict such as "Uploads are making everything wait" or "Your Wi-Fi signal is weak here". - **Latency** updates every second while the section is open, like the ping graph in a call app. **Wi-Fi** shows the signal, band, channel and link rate. - **Test Speed** runs macOS's own speed test when you ask. It tells you first how much data it will use, then how much slower your line gets when it's busy, and whether that's good enough for calls, 4K and game streaming. - **Using the Network** lists the apps sending and receiving the most, now and today, and Performance gains a Network column. - **Data Used** counts what this Mac used today, this week and this month, by day, app and network, while Glade is open. - To tell your networks apart by name, macOS asks for Location access the first time. Everything else works without it. - **Settings > Network** turns the section off, changes the host latency is measured against, and sets how long a speed test runs.
### Your router
- On an AT&T gateway, **Your Network** shows whether your internet line is up and lists the devices on your network with their signal, without a password. - You can add the gateway's Device Access Code. Glade checks it by signing in and keeps it in your Keychain, where no AI ever sees it.
### Little Snitch
- Import a Little Snitch backup on Network, and Glade points out rules that let anything through, duplicates, conflicts, rules for apps you've removed, and ones unused for a year. - **Review with Assistant** explains what to tidy. **Save Cleaned Backup…** writes your backup without the rules it suggested deleting, ready for Little Snitch's own Restore from Backup, which saves your current rules first. The review also names Little Snitch's filters for doing it by hand. - Glade only reads the file you choose. It never touches Little Snitch itself.
### The Assistant remembers
- It follows the conversation, so "and the other one?" or "is it safe to quit that?" is answered in the light of what came before. **New Conversation** starts afresh. - When an answer learns something lasting, such as your internet provider or a problem that keeps coming back, it offers **Remember**. Your notes go with every question after that, and you can change them in **Settings > Assistant**. - **Settings > Protection > Always clear**: name an app you no longer use, and its leftovers and caches are ticked whenever you clean. Leftovers go to the Trash. Personal files, installed apps and anything that can't come back never are, and unattended cleans leave these rules out.
### Command line and AI agents
- `glade network` says where a slowdown is, with the readings behind it. `glade network watch` follows latency second by second and names what was busiest at each spike. `glade network check www.netflix.com` tells a slow service from a slow connection. Also `glade network usage`, `apps`, `router` and `test`, which says how much data it would use before you confirm. - `glade littlesnitch` imports, reviews and writes a cleaned backup; `glade notes` and `glade rules` manage what the Assistant remembers and always clears; `glade ask --continue` follows on from your last question. - Coding agents connected to Glade get the same tools. They see verdicts, numbers and app names, never your network's name, addresses or device names.

### Battery
- A new **Battery** section (called Energy on a Mac without a battery) shows the charge with one plain sentence, such as "On battery, about 6½ hours left", and a chart of the last 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days with time on the charger and asleep shaded. - **Health**, **Power** and **Temperature** each get a panel: how much of its original capacity the battery still holds, how hard the Mac is working, and how warm the battery is. - **Using the most power** lists apps by the energy they've used now, over the last hour, the last 12 hours or since you unplugged, with Quit on the row. It counts processor work only; the screen and graphics chip aren't split between apps. - **Keeping your Mac awake** names what is stopping it sleeping and for how long, including tools like `caffeinate` and simulators playing sound, with Quit or Shut Down beside each. - **While it slept** lists recent sleeps with the charge lost and how often the Mac woke; open one to see why. - The **charge limit** you set in System Settings is shown, with a shortcut to change it there. macOS doesn't let other apps change it. - Six alerts in **Settings > Alerts**: charged past the limit, limit turned off and health below 80% are on; hot while charging, kept awake on battery and a large drain while asleep are off until you switch them on. - **Settings > General > Battery detail**: Simple shows sentences and percentages; Technical adds watts, volts, mAh and cycle counts. - On battery, the menu bar shows the time left and what is using the most power, and Overview has a Battery tile. - Ask the Assistant "What's draining my battery?".
### Uninstall apps
- Storage has an **Apps** section: every app with its size, when you last opened it and where it came from, with big and long-unused ones first. Nothing is ever ticked for you. - Uninstalling moves the app and its own settings, caches and data to the Trash, and **Put Back** returns it all. The inspector shows what goes and what stays, such as data another app shares. - Apps that come with their own uninstaller (Adobe's, for example) get **Open Uninstaller**, because it removes parts Glade can't reach. Apps macOS asks for your password to remove get **Show in Finder**. - In **What's on This Disk**, each folder in your Library says which app uses it, or that no installed app does. From a row you can move a folder to the Trash, uninstall an app or find it in Storage.
### Ask the Assistant to remove things
- Ask it to remove apps by name ("remove the Adobe apps", "uninstall iMovie"). It lists what matches with a reason for each, and a second AI notes what to know first: a subscription that keeps billing, files only that app opens, other apps from the same developer. - Only what you named, and what Glade can remove, starts ticked. **Review and Remove…** opens the usual confirmation; everything goes to the Trash and the card offers **Put Back**. - For this, the AI you chose is sent the names, sizes and last-opened dates of the matching apps. [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) has the full list.
### Command line and AI agents
- New commands: `glade battery`, `glade energy`, `glade awake`, `glade sleeps`, `glade installed` and `glade uninstall` (a dry run unless you add `--confirm`), with matching tools for agents connected to Glade. - `glade ask` lists what it proposes removing and prints the commands to do it. It never removes anything itself. - `glade show <section> --background` changes the window's section without bringing Glade in front of what you're doing.
### Fixed
- In the menu bar, a suggestion's warning ("May be in use by Bitrig") and the memory reading ("Under pressure") are no longer cut off. - In dark mode, cards stand out from the window again instead of blending into it.
### Changed
- With Battery in the sidebar, Assistant is ⌘5 and History is ⌘6.

### Fixed
- In Storage, the group headings (Simulators, Agent Worktrees and so on) scroll along with their items. Before, the top one stuck to the window on a lighter strip with a gap beneath it, which stood out in dark mode. - Searching Storage for something that isn't there shows "No Results" across the whole list, with the Free Up bar at the bottom where it belongs, instead of a lighter band and the bar floating halfway up.
